_comment: Which colour token is painted on which, and what WCAG 2.1 AA asks of that combination.
A fact about the design rather than about any one file, so it is declared here and read twice:
by scripts/contrast.py, which resolves the tokens out of frontend/src/styles/site.scss and
writes docs/verification/contrast.json; and by /app/design, which resolves them out of the
running page and computes the same ratios in the browser, in whichever theme is on.
Those two answers are compared in frontend/tests/e2e/design.spec.ts.
It lives under frontend/src/ because that is the only tree the reader's build can import from:
frontend/Dockerfile's build context is ./frontend, so nothing under docs/ exists at build time.
AA is 4.5:1 on text; large text and non-text parts of a control are 3:1 (1.4.3, 1.4.11). Where a
pair is painted in both roles the stricter number is used. requires: null means measured and
reported but held to no ratio — see reason.

pairs.usage: body text on the page
body text on a panel or summary box
text typed into a form control
a menu row under the pointer or the focus ring — the navbar's dropdowns, both display switches, the account rows
secondary text: notes, source credit, captions
secondary text inside a panel
a link in running text
a link inside a panel
a link on a form control
error text
the repealed / omitted badge's own text
text inside a selected sort or facet pill
pairs.note: The selected sort option and the applied facet are filled pills. Their text is --danger-ink for the reason that token exists: text on a filled colour cannot inherit --ink, which inverts with the theme while the fill under it does not.

pairs.usage: an insertion in a redline, and the current-release marker
pairs.note: The brand reserves one green for version semantics and puts it nowhere else (ADR-0052). It is read as text and as a 3px rule, so it is held to the text ratio, the stricter of the two.

pairs.usage: the same, on a panel
the boundary of an input, select or textarea
a control's boundary against the page
a control's boundary inside a panel
the focus ring, and the edge of a highlighted provision
the focus ring over a panel
dividers, the edge of a note, table cell borders
pairs.reason: SC 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of visual information required to identify user interface components and states — a control's boundary. A divider between two paragraphs identifies nothing: remove it entirely and the page still says everything it said. Holding it to 3:1 anyway would put every hairline on the site at #949494 or darker, a visibly heavier reader bought for no conformance gain. --edge is the half of the old --rule that does carry meaning, and it is held to the ratio.

pairs.usage: a divider drawn on a panel
